title: Rational Picard descent along a torus torsor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a smooth separated finite-type geometrically integral $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $T$ a $k$-torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], and $q:Y\to X$ a $T$-torsor for the fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]: $q$ is faithfully flat of finite presentation, with a $T$-action over $X$ for which $(y,t)\mapsto(y,yt)$ is an isomorphism $Y\times_kT\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every invertible module $L$ on $Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there exist an integer $c\geq1$ and an invertible module $M$ on $X$ with an isomorphism $q^*M\simeq L^{\otimes c}$.

source.place: Proposition 6.10 (Picard sequence for a torus torsor), finite Galois splitting, and the norm construction for invertible modules.

proof.text: By the definition of a torus, $T_{\bar k}\simeq\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r$ for some $r\geq0$. This split torus is affine and of finite type, with coordinate algebra $\bar k[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ (generated by $t_i,t_i^{-1}$). The field-extension covering lemma makes $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ an fpqc singleton. Apply fpqc descent of affineness, local finite type and quasi-compactness to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus $T$ is an affine finite-type group of multiplicative type, so the character antiduality theorem applies in the next step.

source.place: Tags 02L5 (lemma-descending-property-affine), 02KX (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type), 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact); torus definition from Milne, Definition 12.14.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] to $T$. Its finite separable splitting assertion gives $K/k$ finite separable and $T_K\simeq D_K(M)$. Its scalar-extension and character-identification clauses identify $M$ with $X^*(T_{\bar k})\simeq X^*(\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r)=\mathbf Z^r$. Here $D_F(\mathbf Z^r)=\mathbf G_{m,F}^r$ directly: $e_{(n_i)}\mapsto\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$ identifies the group algebra and its coproduct with the Laurent coordinate algebra. The inverse-character clause of the same theorem then gives the asserted character identification. Hence $T_K\simeq\mathbf G_{m,K}^r$. Put $d=[K:k]$, which is a positive integer since $K$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over $k$. No Galois enlargement is needed.

source.place: Theorem 12.23 and the finite Galois splitting used in the proof of Corollary 12.25, printed pp.239--240; character identification of Theorem 12.9.

proof.text: Form $X_K,Y_K$ and the Cartesian square with horizontal maps $q_K:Y_K\to X_K$, $q:Y\to X$ and projections $b:Y_K\to Y$, $a:X_K\to X$. Smooth base change and separated finite-type base change show that $X_K$ is a smooth separated finite-type $K$-scheme. By the fppf-covering calculus (including its scheme comparison), the singleton $q_K$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation; the finite-presentation base-change lemma gives finite presentation itself. Base-changing the given action and its inverse torsor isomorphism gives $Y_K\times_KT_K\simeq Y_K\times_{X_K}Y_K$: both composites remain identities by the fibre-product universal property. Transporting the action along the split-torus isomorphism therefore makes $q_K$ a split torus torsor with all the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback].

source.place: Tag 021O (lemma-fppf), part (3); morphisms.tex Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); schemes.tex Tag 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence); morphisms.tex Tags 01T4 and 01TS (finite type and finite presentation base change); groupoids.tex following Definition 0498 (definition-pseudo-torsor).

proof.text:
On inverse images of opens trivializing $L$, its tensor inverse image $b^*L$ is $\mathcal O_{Y_K}\otimes_{b^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}b^{-1}\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_{Y_K}$, so it is invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback] over $K$ to $b^*L$. It gives an invertible module $N$ on $X_K$ and $q_K^*N\simeq b^*L$. Choose an invertible module $M$ on $X$ representing $\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,X}([N])$. The norm lemma supplies such a line class, its compatibility with $q$, and its degree formula on $Y$. Consequently
$$[q^*M]=q^*\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,X}([N])=\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Y}([q_K^*N])=\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Y}([b^*L])=[L^{\otimes d}].$$
Equality of these isomorphism classes means $q^*M\simeq L^{\otimes d}$. Take $c=d\geq1$. Geometric integrality of $X$ is not needed by the split-torus input, and remains an allowed hypothesis of the item.

Step 1: the torus definition plus lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover make Spec k̄→Spec k flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and the fpqc descent nodes (affine, locally finite type, quasi-compact) then make T affine of finite type and of multiplicative type, which is what the antiduality node needs. Step 2: the antiduality node gives a finite separable splitting T_L≅D_L(M); its scalar-extension and inverse-character clauses give M≅X^*(G_m^r)=Z^r; checked against Milne iAG2017 Thm 12.23 and Cor 12.25. Step 3: X_K is smooth, separated and of finite type; q_K is flat, lfp and surjective via clauses (4)→(2)→(4) of lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus, and of finite presentation by qcqs-permanence (3); the torsor isomorphism base-changes on the correct fibre product. All hypotheses of lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback hold. Step 4: with h=q and Z=Y, the norm node gives [q^*Nm N]=[Nm q_K^*N]=[Nm b^*L]=[L^{⊗d}], so c=d. New node lem-sfb-finite-field-picard-norm-base-change: true by Stacks 0BCY (Norm(π^*N)=N^d) and 0BD2 (canonical norm commutes with arbitrary base change), since p_Z is finite locally free of rank d. Tested on empty Z, K=k, C/R, purely inseparable K and nonreduced Z. Forms B1–B5 hold. Not a duplicate: lem-pur-finite-flat-kummer-norm-degree is Noetherian-only with no base-change naturality; the function-norm and frame-gluing nodes give no naturality on classes. It is not a restatement of the item.
